Inspection for the cable testing (Continuity Test) for Access Control System cable  (Door Contacts & SACPs) at Opera House Building, Level-00 Part-2 Grid lines Aa-F/05-12a as per the attached highlighted drawing. (.)

Witnessed the performed initial cable continuity testing for Access Control System homerun cables associated with door contact monitoring and indication to the Access Control Panel located in the IDF Room at L00, Part 02 Area. The testing was conducted to support the closure of Site Observation Reports (SORs) related to previously installed cables that were pulled without prior conduit inspection and to verify the integrity and continuity of the installed control cables, accepted with comments.
Remarks: The following requirements shall be compiled prior to RFI Cable Testing 
1. Permanent cable identification tags shall be provided and installed at both cable ends in accordance with the approved IFC shop drawings, schematic diagrams, and project labeling standards. The tag labels shall clearly indicate the cable origin and destination, including the corresponding room number and/or door number.
2. Updated and approved IFC shop drawings, cable schedules, and schematic diagrams shall be available and attached during cable testing activities to facilitate verification of cable routing, termination points, and test results.
3. All test instruments utilized for continuity testing shall possess valid calibration certificates, and copies of the certificates shall be made available for review prior to commencement of testing.
4. Test records clearly identify the tested cable reference number, source location, destination location, test method used, date of testing, and witnessing personnel.
5. Any discrepancies identified during testing, including open circuits, incorrect terminations, or cable identification issues, shall be rectified and retested prior to acceptance during the final test.

Mockup Inspection for Installation of Lighting fixture (L1) for Normal lighting system (Lighting fixture-01 points) at Opera Building, Level-B2, Part-02, Grid line C-Ha/12a-02b as per attached highlighted drawing.

RFI was rejected, the mock-up installation does not comply with the project requirements for the following reasons:

1.The installed flexible conduit is not a liquid-tight type.
IFC detail drawings require the use of liquid-tight flexible metallic conduit (LFMC) for fixture connections in the basement area.
Considering the possibility of water leakage, condensation, and sprinkler system discharge, liquid-tight protection is required to prevent moisture ingress, note that the lighting fixtures are specified as IP66 rated and installed in the basement environment where exposure to moisture is possible and the fixture contains electronic DALI control gear/ballast, which is susceptible to damage and malfunction if exposed to moisture.

3. The installed support does not comply with the IFC detail drawings. IFC details require supports fabricated from 25 mm conduit hangers/supports.

Inspection for the Storage & Preservation for Generators GPC1565-UL & GPC1845-UL (Opera Building & Car park)  in Opera House Building, Level-00, Part-03 as per attached ITP and Checklist. (.)

Field inspection confirms heavy accumulation of fine sand and civil concrete dust directly on the machine bodies, auxiliary boxes, and inside the alternator ventilation components.

Leaving construction dust inside the unit creates an immediate technical hazard. Fine dust absorbs ambient humidity, creating a conductive bridge across the copper windings that leads to electrical tracking and shorts. Per international standards like IEEE 43, conducting a routine insulation test (such as a 500V Megger test) on a contaminated winding can cause permanent, catastrophic phase-to-ground short circuits.

The current flexible tarpaulin setups are inadequate as they are unsealed and easily bypassed by wind and dust. The following corrective actions are strictly required before resubmission:

1. Small Generator Unit (Open Structural Zone)

Enclosure: Erect rigid temporary hoarding (e.g., plywood panels) on the open sides to eliminate the wind tunnel effect forcing sand under the covers.

Ventilation: Maintain a double-tarpaulin labyrinth vent at the base to allow internal heater warmth to rise and escape safely without drawing in sand at the base.

2. Large Generator Unit (Loading Bay Zone)

Isolation: Construct a dust-tight, floor-to-ceiling plywood partition around the scaffolding frame to completely isolate the asset from local road traffic sand, concrete pouring, and mechanical grinding dust.

Deep Cleaning: Meticulously vacuum and clean all internal generator components and windings using approved electrical contact cleaners prior to re-inspection.

Steel angle installation inspection for metal decking at gridline near Fc-Kc/ 01c-12 at part 05 level 02 of
opera building (as per attached highlighted drawing)

The RFI has been **rejected** due to the contractor’s failure to close out the following comments within the specified timeframe, notwithstanding that the RFI was inspected on **three separate occasions**:

1. The alignment of the installed expansion bolts is not in accordance with the approved drawings and specified tolerances; necessary realignment and corrective works are required.
2. Complete technical details for the angle-to-beam connection shall be submitted.
3. The identified gap between the angle section and the concrete wall shall be rectified to achieve full, continuous, and uniform bearing/contact.
4. Pull-out testing of the expansion bolts shall be arranged through an approved third-party testing agency, and the required testing frequency (per 100 installed bolts) shall be confirmed in compliance with the project specifications.
5. All expansion bolts shall be installed perpendicular to both the angle section and the concrete wall surface, and any irregular gaps between nuts and washers shall be eliminated.
6. The embedment depth of the installed expansion bolts is less than the minimum requirement indicated in the approved drawings; compliant embedment length shall be provided.
7. Justification shall be submitted for the excessive number of holes observed in the angle sections, along with an approved method statement for the proper closure and treatment of all unused holes.

Steel reinforcement & embedded items installation inspection for metal deck at grid line Kc-N/ 01c-05c at part 5 level 01 of opera building (as per attached highlighted drawing)

The RFI has been **rejected** due to the contractor’s failure to address the following comments within the stipulated timeframe, despite the RFI being inspected on **three occasions**:

1. All gaps at metal deck joints—including interfaces between metal decks and adjacent walls—shall be properly sealed in accordance with the approved details.
2. Excessive foam applied at sealed joints shall be removed, and a neat, controlled application shall be ensured in compliance with project specifications.
3. All foreign materials shall be completely removed from the work area, including plastic debris, rebar caps, foam, timber, and other loose items.
4. Edge reinforcement of T12 @ 300 mm c/c with proper hooks shall be provided strictly as per the approved shop drawings.
5. Additional and/or diagonal reinforcement around all MEP sleeves shall be installed in accordance with the approved structural details.
6. The approved MEP RFI relevant to the inspected works shall be submitted and made available.
7. T12 @ 200 mm c/c dowel bars shall be provided in the seaside wall to ensure proper splicing with the metal deck reinforcement, as indicated in the approved drawings.
8. All loose and unsound concrete at wall construction joints shall be removed.
9. Adequate spacer blocks shall be provided beneath 32 mm diameter reinforcement bars (fire reinforcement) to maintain the specified concrete cover.
10. The missing additional reinforcement at the north side shall be installed in full compliance with the approved drawings and bar bending schedules.
Accordingly, the RFI remains **denied** until all the above items are fully rectified and a follow-up inspection is requested.

Installation Inspection of shear studs near gridlines L-Kc/08c, at part 05, level 01

Rejection Reasons – Inspection Observations:
1. Hammer Test Failures: Sixteen studs failed completely within the second hammer strike, confirming lack of fusion between the weld and the shear studs.
2. Visual Defects: Most shear studs show discontinuities and lack a complete 360° flash, indicating insufficient or improper welding.
3. Surface Condition: All studs were inadequately cleaned and display visible rust and welding spatters.
4. Ferrule Retention: Some studs were found with ceramic ferrules still in place after welding.
5. Unauthorized Welding: Additional studs were welded manually using SMAW with E7018 electrodes without prior approval.

Installation Inspection of shear studs near gridlines J-K in part 04, level 01 of Opera Building (As per attached highlighted drawing) (level 01)

Rejection Reasons are mentioned below,
Inspection Observations:
1. Visual inspection revealed that most shear studs exhibit discontinuities and lack a complete 360° flash, indicating insufficient or improper welding.
2. Random bend tests resulted in complete failure of the studs within the second hammer strike, confirming lack of fusion between the weld and the shear studs.
3. The stud material (SWRCH18A) does not comply with the project specification requirements of ASTM A108, Grades 1015, 1017, or 1020 cold-finished carbon steel.
4. Horizontal spacing (pitch) between the studs is not referenced in the submitted drawing.
5. All studs were found inadequately cleaned and show visible signs of rust.
6. Touch-up painting has not been carried out.

Document Deficiencies:
1. Approved shop drawing is not available.
2. Shear stud welding ITP has not been submitted.
3. SPP for shear stud welding is pending submission.
4. Approved WPS for shear stud welding is not available.
5. Qualification approval for the stud welding operator is not evidenced.
6. MIR approval for base material (beam) is not attached.
7. MIR approval for stud material is not attached.
8. MIR approval for ceramic ferrule is not attached.
9. Mock-up approval for shear stud welding has not been obtained.
10. Calibration certificates for Welding machine and gun not evidenced.

Inspection Request for Assembly and Installation of Hanger & support and HVAC Metal Duct Grid line Hc-Jc/03c-07c Part 05 B2 Opere House as per highlighted drawing.

This RFI has been rejected due to the following observations,
Physical Inspection Observations:
1. The installed and submitted section lacks the take-off installation as specified in the approved shop drawing.
2. The horizontal coordinates or positioning of the installed duct could not be verified due to the absence of dimensional data in the approved shop drawing.
3. The clearance between the installed HVAC duct and adjacent cable trays does not meet the specification requirements. A gap of only 30mm was observed in both vertical and horizontal directions, which is below the minimum clearance specified.
4. One of the installed support edges was found to have visible rust, indicating that touch-up coating was not applied as required by the specification. 
5. The installed ductwork lacks proper identification markings, which are required for traceability and verification in accordance with project specifications.
6. An unapproved zinc spray (soudal) was used for touch-up coating on galvanized supports.
7. The ductwork installation is insufficiently braced, resulting in lateral sway and compromised structural stability/rigidity.
8. One of the hanger supports is positioned too close to the duct joint.

Documentation Review Observations:
1. Neither coordination drawings nor BIM-extracted models have been provided to verify compliance with adjacent other service clearance requirements. The absence of these documents prevents confirmation that the installation meets the specified spatial allowances. 
2. The horizontal coordinates or positioning of the installed duct are not referenced in the approved shop drawing, nor supported by BIM data. Furthermore, no evidence—such as an approved surveyor’s report—has been provided by the contractor to confirm compliance with this requirement.
3. The detailed HVAC installation drawing (Ref: JOH-ICD-S5-056-XXX-XX-SD-ME-(010001:010010)) was not attached to the submitted RFI.
4. The qualification documents for the duct installer were not attached to the submitted RFI.
5. The qualification documents for the duct insulator were not included in the submitted RFI.
